sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.subHeading: How are spaces handled?

content.text: Letters are separated by a single space, words by / (or three spaces). When decoding, both conventions are recognized.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.subHeading: Does it support prosigns?

content.text: The tool supports the standard ITU Morse code alphabet (A-Z, 0-9). Prosigns (procedural signals like -.-. for 'break') are not built in but can be entered manually.

The Data URI Generator converts files or text into Data URIs (RFC 2397) that can be embedded directly in HTML, CSS, or JavaScript. A Data URI has the format data:[][;base64],. For text, the tool URL-encodes the content; for binary files, it Base64-encodes. The resulting URI can replace external file references with inline data.

sections.heading: How to Use Data URI Generator

items: Step 1: Paste text or upload a file to convert.
Step 2: The tool detects the content type and generates the appropriate Data URI.
Step 3: Copy the Data URI for use in src, href, or CSS url() attributes.

content.text: Data URIs eliminate HTTP requests by embedding resources directly in HTML or CSS. They're useful for small icons, fonts, and images that reduce page load time by avoiding additional network round trips. They're also essential for email HTML where external images may be blocked.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.subHeading: When should I use Data URIs vs external files?

content.text: Use Data URIs for small resources (<5KB) like icons, logos, and fonts. For larger files, external references are better because Data URIs increase HTML file size and can't be cached separately.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.subHeading: What content types are supported?

content.text: Any MIME type: image/png, image/svg+xml, image/jpeg, font/woff2, text/css, etc. The tool auto-detects the type from the input.

The URL Slug Generator converts text into URL-friendly slugs by lowercasing, replacing spaces with hyphens, removing special characters, and collapsing consecutive hyphens. The resulting string is safe for use in URL paths: My Blog Post: Tips & Tricks! becomes my-blog-post-tips-tricks.

sections.heading: How to Use URL Slug Generator

items: Step 1: Paste a title, heading, or any text into the input area.
Step 2: Click Transform. The URL slug appears in the output.

content.text: Every CMS, blog platform, and static site generator needs slugs for URL paths. Manually creating slugs for hundreds of articles is tedious and inconsistent. This tool generates consistent, SEO-friendly slugs that work across all web servers and don't require URL encoding.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.subHeading: How are special characters handled?

content.text: Special characters (!, @, #, &, etc.) are removed entirely. Spaces become hyphens. Consecutive hyphens are collapsed to a single hyphen. Leading/trailing hyphens are trimmed.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.subHeading: Does it handle Unicode characters?

content.text: Basic Unicode letters (accented characters) are kept. Characters that can't be represented in a URL path are stripped. For full Unicode URL support (internationalized domain names), use the Punycode Converter instead.
